Casually

/KAZH-oo-uh-lee/ - the stress falls on the first syllable · adverb

Hear It

What It Means

Casually means in a relaxed, offhand, or unconcerned manner.

Between bites of his sandwich, the crane operator casually described lifting a grand piano to a ninth-floor window, as though it were nothing at all.

Worked Example

On her first day, the intern found herself alone in the elevator with the CEO. Rather than freeze, she casually asked how his morning was going, mentioned an article of his she had liked, and stepped off at her floor with a wave — as relaxed as if she had been chatting with a roommate.

Casually is the right word because it describes her easy, offhand manner and nothing more. It is not carelessly, which would mean her attention actually failed: a surgeon can chat casually while operating flawlessly, but the moment she skips a step she is working carelessly.

Antonyms

How Strong Is It? — lightly → casually → carelessly → recklessly

lightly vs. casually

lightly vs. casually: To take a remark lightly is merely not to weigh it down; casually goes a step further, wearing plain ease in how you speak or act.

carelessly vs. casually

carelessly vs. casually: Carelessly goes beyond casually and becomes a fault: the casual cook chats while stirring, the careless one lets the pot burn.

recklessly vs. casually

recklessly vs. casually: Recklessly sits at the far end of the ladder — not just unbothered but courting danger, like the driver who passes on a blind curve.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — casu

Root — casu: chance, a falling (Latin cadere, to fall)

Suffix — -al

Suffix — -al: relating to

Suffix — -ly

Suffix — -ly: in the manner of

Put it together

Put it together: Casu (chance, a falling) + -al (relating to) + -ly (in the manner of) = in a manner that takes things as they fall. Latin casus meant 'a fall of the dice, a chance event,' so doing something casually is letting it happen as chance brings it — unplanned, unforced, easy.

Use the root in a new word: occasion

Use the root in a new word: occasion: The retirement dinner was a rare occasion for the whole crew to sit at one table.

Root Check

Word Choice

neutral / conversational

Casually describes a relaxed, offhand manner and passes no judgment on the result. Its trap is carelessly, which condemns: casual work can still be flawless, while careless work by definition is not. Its cluster-mate nonchalant is the adjective for the same easy surface — a nonchalant shrug is a shrug given casually.
